## Key terms

{{< glossary account authentication single-sign-on file folder file-path file-extension file-size cloud-storage synchronization backup >}}

## 2.1 Digital identity and the university account

An **account** identifies you to a service. **Authentication** proves that you
own it, with factors you **know** (password), **have** (phone code) or **are**
(fingerprint). **Single sign-on (SSO)** lets one university sign-in open
e-mail, the e-learning platform, cloud storage and office apps. It is safer
and simpler, but a stolen password opens everything — so on shared lab
computers: sign out, never save passwords, use a private window, lock the
screen.

![Single sign-on with the university account.](images/sso.png){width=84%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Accounts and sign-in"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="something you see"}
A password.
:   something you know

A code sent to your phone.
:   something you have

A fingerprint.
:   something you are

One sign-in for e-mail, e-learning and cloud storage.
:   single sign-on

The main risk of single sign-on.
:   a stolen password opens every service

The habit at the end of every lab session.
:   sign out of every service
:::
:::

## 2.2 Files, folders and paths

Storage is a **tree** of **folders** and **files**. A **path** is a file's
address: `C:\Users\Sara\Documents\…` on Windows, `/Users/sara/Documents/…` on
a Mac. An **absolute path** starts at the root; a **relative path** starts at
the current folder, and `..` means the parent folder. The **extension**
(`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.png`, `.exe`) tells the type — show extensions, because
`invoice.pdf.exe` is a program. Sizes: 1 byte = 8 bits; KB, MB, GB, TB.
Manufacturers count in powers of 1000, many systems in powers of 1024 — so a
"128 GB" phone shows about 119 GB.

![A folder tree for course work, with the path of one file.](images/folder-tree.png){width=80%}

![File types and size units.](images/file-types.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/path-finder.html" poster="sims/path-finder.png" title="Path Finder: files, folders and paths" kind="game" height="620" >}}

::: {.match extra="slash (/)|a document|128 GB"}
The separator used in Windows paths.
:   backslash (\\)

A path that starts at the root.
:   absolute path

:   the parent folder

## 2.3 Naming and organising files

Good names are **descriptive and consistent**, avoid spaces and special
characters (use `-` or `_`), write dates as **YYYY-MM-DD** so that alphabetical
order is also time order, and number versions (`v01`, `v02`) instead of
"final". Folders: shallow, the same structure for every project.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Good names"}
Choose the best answer.

::: {.match extra="New Document (3).docx|cv final.docx|21-10-2026"}
The date format that sorts in time order.
:   YYYY-MM-DD

What to use instead of "final", "final2", "final3".
:   version numbers (v01, v02)

What to use instead of spaces in a file name.
:   a hyphen or an underscore

The best name for the Digital Skills week 1 CV, made on 21 October 2026.
:   2026-10-21_DS_week01_cv_v01.docx
:::
:::

## 2.4 Cloud storage, synchronization and backup

**Cloud storage** keeps files on a provider's servers, reachable from any
device, within a **quota**. **Synchronization** keeps copies identical — so a
deletion or a mistake is copied everywhere. A **backup** is an independent copy
for restoring data. Recycle bins and **version history** help for a limited
time; the **3-2-1 rule** protects important work: 3 copies, 2 kinds of storage,
1 off-site.

![Synchronization copies mistakes; a backup does not.](images/sync-backup.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Sync or backup?"}
Choose the right term.

::: {.match extra="compression"}
A deletion on one device appears on all your devices.
:   synchronization

An independent copy kept to restore lost data.
:   backup

The rule "3 copies, 2 kinds of storage, 1 off-site".
:   the 3-2-1 rule

The feature that keeps earlier versions of a file.
:   version history

The maximum storage space a user is allowed.
:   quota
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Sara's media project {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Sara (user `sara` on a Mac) prepares a project for Digital Media. Her folder
`Documents/Courses/Digital-Media/week-01` contains 3 videos of 450 MB and 60
photos of 2.5 MB. The e-learning platform accepts at most 1 GB (1 000 MB) per
submission. The folder is synchronized with her university cloud storage, and
every Sunday she copies it to a USB drive that she keeps at home.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Sara's project (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1 050 MB|it fits|the synchronized laptop"}
The total size of the videos and photos.
:   1 500 MB

Does it fit in one submission?
:   no, 500 MB too large

The absolute path of `trailer.mp4` in that folder.
:   /Users/sara/Documents/Courses/Digital-Media/week-01/trailer.mp4

She deletes the folder on the lab computer by mistake. Where can she restore it first?
:   the cloud recycle bin

Her USB copy at home, in the 3-2-1 rule.
:   the off-site copy
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Lab tasks · Set up your digital workspace"}
1. Sign in to the lab computer and to your university account.
2. Open the university cloud storage in the browser.
3. Create the folders `Courses/Digital-Skills/week-01` and one folder for each
   of your other courses.
4. Save your DigComp profile from lesson 1 in `week-01` with a name that
   follows the rules of §2.3.
5. Rename the file once (`v02`), then open its version history.
6. Delete the file, restore it from the recycle bin, and check that it is back.
7. Sign out of every service and of the browser.
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Account + authentication (know, have, are); SSO: one sign-in, many services.
- Storage is a tree; a path is an address; absolute vs relative; `..` = parent.
- Read extensions; 1000 vs 1024 explains "missing" gigabytes.
- Names: descriptive, no spaces, YYYY-MM-DD, v01.
- Sync copies mistakes; a backup does not; 3-2-1.
